data.body:
Change 2620 patchset 2 is GREEN on both merge gates: LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1
(https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/33875748018). Not submitted and the ticket is
not closed — left for the caller.

Patchset 2 fixed two real advisories from ps1's review:

1. `observability.sh` §2e published `disk_used_percent` unconditionally. `df` on an unmounted
   mount point answers for the filesystem CONTAINING it, so an unmounted scratch volume would
   have reported ROOT's usage under `mount=/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch` — a real number about
   the wrong volume, leaving `rebar-gate-scratch-disk-high` reading healthy while scratch was
   gone, or paging "scratch is full" during a root incident. The publish is now gated on the
   mountedness heartbeat; silence is the honest reading and the alarm's
   `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` pages on it. Pinned by a new test.

2. The recovery block in `review-bot-ops.md` recreated only the PROOF marker, which was worse
   than incomplete — `touch <mount>/.gate-scratch-mounted` while the volume is unmounted lands
   the file in the underlying ROOT directory and tells the guard the volume is mounted when it
   is not. That is the silent fallback to root this story removes, performed by its own
   recovery procedure. Recovery now recreates the declaration unconditionally and the proof
   only behind `mountpoint -q`, and explains that the declaration is the marker that is easy
   to lose without noticing (root-resident, so an instance replacement drops it while the
   volume and its proof survive, and the guard is then simply off).

## Follow-up worth a ticket (advisory on ps2, deliberately NOT in scope here)

The refusal guards `gate_admission()`, which wraps plan-review and completion-verifier. The
review-bot's per-review `reviewbot-*` clone (`review_bot/voter.py`) does NOT pass through it,
so on a declared-but-unmounted volume that path still clones — onto root — rather than
refusing. This story's AC3 only required the clone tempdir to RESOLVE to the scratch volume
(it does, via `TMPDIR`), and ADR 0112 puts the refusal at gate admission, so this is a real
gap in the ADR's coverage rather than a defect in the change. It also interacts with ADR 0069:
the code-review path must treat this as a retryable deferral, never an `LLM-Review -1`, which
is exactly the carve-out S6 had to make for congestion. Worth a sibling ticket under the epic.

Two other ps1 advisories were answered rather than changed, with reasoning recorded on the
Gerrit change: the container's write access to the declaration marker (the stack's existing
root-container posture, not something this bind creates, and belongs with container hardening)
and the text assertion pinning observability and the refusal to ONE notion of "mounted"
(a same-source constraint that behaviour cannot observe; `mountpoint` and the proof marker can
legitimately disagree inside a container, and monitoring that disagrees with enforcement reads
healthy while every gate refuses).
